title: Non-blocking follow-up from PR #174 review (frontend-volume-indicators-chart)
description: Tracked non-blocking findings from pr-reviewer's review of PR #174 (frontend-volume-indicators-chart), recorded here per CLAUDE.md's 'every non-blocking finding becomes a tracked task' rule so they aren't lost once that PR merges. None of these affect runtime correctness of the shipped chart/legend/help content -- confirmed via a live browser walkthrough (correct two-pane rendering, no console/network errors, accurate MetricHelp text) and a full coverage/lint/type/e2e pass -- so none blocked acceptance of PR #174.

checklist.step: VolumeIndicatorsChart.tsx's doc comment (and this task's own 'no zero-baseline' decisions entry) incorrectly claims OBV/A-D 'are constructed to start at exactly 0 on the first plotted bar'. In fact backend/app/api/routers/stocks.py computes obv_full/accumulation_distribution_full over the ticker's entire untrimmed daily_ohlcv and only slices by from_index for the requested range -- confirmed live (GET /api/stocks/AAPL/indicators?range=1y returns obv=164800429500.0 on the first bar, and the browser walkthrough's default-range screenshot shows the OBV y-axis spanning ~163.75B-165.25B, nowhere near 0). The 0-anchor documented in backend-indicator-obv-ad's own decisions applies only to the ticker's absolute first historical bar (i.e. range=max), not to the first bar of whatever window is currently displayed -- the default range is 1y (PriceChart.tsx's DEFAULT_RANGE), so this misstatement affects the common case, not just an edge case. The practical conclusion (no zero-baseline reference line) still holds for an independent reason (a windowed slice's own arbitrary carried-over starting value still isn't a meaningful sign-based threshold), but the stated rationale and comment should be corrected to avoid misleading a future maintainer who trusts it at face value.

metricHelpContent.ts's cumulativeVolumeSeriesInterpretation() detects whether the latest bar is 'currently at its own window high/low' via reference equality (`last === highest` / `last === lowest`) against the result of `series.reduce(...)`, rather than by value. Since the reduce uses a strict `>`/`<` comparison, an exact tie between the latest bar and an earlier bar in the window resolves `highest`/`lowest` to the earlier occurrence, so `last` is a different array entry even though its value is identical -- the generated help text then falls into the 'not at either extreme' branch and misstates the window's high/low instead of noting the current bar is (jointly) at that extreme. Narrow edge case for a real-valued cumulative series, but worth a value-based comparison (`last.value === highest.value`) instead.

StockCharts.test.tsx (unchanged by this PR) was not extended to assert that VolumeIndicatorsChart is actually wired correctly inside the composed StockCharts page (e.g. correct range/enabled props, canvas presence, hide/restore on interval toggle) the way it already does for OscillatorChart -- only the standalone VolumeIndicatorsChart.test.tsx exercises the component in isolation. Coverage numbers are unaffected (StockCharts.tsx is 100% covered), but a future edit that silently breaks the StockCharts->VolumeIndicatorsChart wiring (e.g. swapping range/enabled props) would not be caught by this suite. Consider adding an integration-level assertion or two.

decisions.decision: Fixed all three findings as described: corrected VolumeIndicatorsChart.tsx's doc comment to state the real 0-anchor behavior (only at the ticker's absolute first historical bar / range=max, not the first bar of whatever window is requested, confirmed against backend/app/api/routers/stocks.py's own obv_full/accumulation_distribution_full-then-slice behavior); switched cumulativeVolumeSeriesInterpretation's high/low-tie check in metricHelpContent.ts from array reference equality to value equality; and added two integration tests to StockCharts.test.tsx mirroring the existing OscillatorChart wiring tests (range mirroring, hide/restore on interval toggle) for VolumeIndicatorsChart. Implemented as part of a batched PR (task/frontend-followups-batch-1) alongside four other small stocks-page follow-up tasks.
decisions.rationale: All three were small, well-scoped, low-risk fixes exactly as described by the review findings -- no reason to defer any of them. The doc-comment fix keeps a future maintainer from trusting a stated rationale that's actually wrong even though its practical conclusion (no zero-baseline line) still holds for a different, correct reason. The value-based tie comparison is a one-line change with no behavior change for the non-tied case. The StockCharts.test.tsx additions directly mirror the existing OscillatorChart pattern in the same file, so there was an established template to follow rather than a novel test design.

review.notes: Reviewed as part of PR #207, a batched PR covering five followup tasks (this one plus frontend-trend-strength-chart-followups, frontend-divergence-markers-followups, frontend-tide-region-chart-shading-followups, frontend-profit-target-display-followups); see this PR's own COMMENTED-type review for the full cross-task verification detail. This task's own tie-detection fix (cumulativeVolumeSeriesInterpretation switching from reference equality to `.value` equality) was hand-verified with a constructed tie case: series [{5,d1},{3,d2},{5,d3=last}] -- old code's `reduce` with strict `>` keeps the EARLIER occurrence on a tie, so `highest={5,d1}` while `last={5,d3}`; reference equality (`last === highest`) is false, incorrectly falling into the 'not at either extreme' branch and reporting a misleading high/low pair, while the new `.value`-based check correctly reports 'currently at its own highest point'. Genuine fix, not a regression. The new StockCharts.test.tsx integration tests correctly mirror the existing OscillatorChart wiring-test pattern. Full frontend suite (690 tests, 99.72% coverage) and backend suite (929 tests, 99.94% coverage) pass; eslint/tsc/mypy clean. No findings specific to this task's own change.
